items.title: Tinubu to First Lady at 66: You’re my truest friend
items.description: By Johnbosco Agbakwuru ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has celebrated the 66th birthday of his wife, First Lady Senator Oluremi Tinubu, describing her as his “truest friend and confidante” and declaring that, if life gave him another chance, he would choose the same path that led him to her. Tinubu, in a birthday message on Sunday, addressed the First Lady as “Oluremi mi” and wrote: “Today, I celebrate the woman who has walked beside me with patience, grace and uncommon courage.” The President invoked Yoruba wisdom and scripture, quoting the proverb, “Ìyàwó rere ni adé ọkọ rẹ̀” — “A good wife is her husband’s crown” — and adding that the Book of Proverbs, which she knows “far better than I do,” also speaks eloquently of the worth of a virtuous woman. Tinubu credited his wife with sharing his burdens and understanding him in ways few others could. “The burdens that were mine to bear often found their way onto your shoulders. The thoughts I could not put into words somehow found their way to you,” he wrote. He recalled her composure during difficult periods, saying: “In difficult times, when the future was uncertain, you stayed calm beside me and prayed with me. Through all these years, you have remained the one who truly understands me.” The President also praised her honesty, particularly her willingness to tell him difficult truths. “I call you my truest friend and confidante because you speak the truth plainly, even on the days I would rather not hear it,” he said. “After a demanding day, you wait until we are alone before telling me what I need to hear. I have always cherished you for that honesty.” Tinubu highlighted the First Lady’s role in shaping their family and faith life, saying their children and grandchildren had grown under the influence of her prayers, values of faith and kindness. “Our home bears the lasting imprint of your devotion. Our children and grandchildren have grown beneath the shelter of your prayers. They carry your values of faith and kindness wherever life takes them,” he said. The President also praised her public service and compassion, saying Nigerians knew her for her kindness, generosity and steadfast faith. “I have watched you touch lives quietly and consistently, offering hope and support to those in need,” he said. Tinubu traced her humanitarian activities from their years in Lagos to her current national platform. “From the New Era Foundation during our years in the saddle in Lagos to the Renewed Hope Initiative today, your care has reached many young boys and girls, widows, elderly citizens, and women farmers across the country,” he said. He singled out her advocacy for people affected by tuberculosis and other diseases, describing her as “a compassionate advocate and a determined champion.” Tinubu further said his wife’s compassion transcended ethnic, regional and religious boundaries. “I know the prayers you offer for people whose names you may never know. I also know many whom you have helped without ever meeting them. For you, compassion has never recognised the boundaries of tribe, region or religion,” he said. Reflecting on their years together, the President said their shared experiences had strengthened their relationship. “A long journey teaches a man the true value of a good partner. We have travelled a long road together. I think of the difficult decisions we talked through for hours and the sacrifices no one else saw. Laughter and prayer carried us through many of them,” he said. Tinubu ended the tribute with a declaration of enduring love and commitment. “If life returned me to the beginning, I would choose the same road that led me to you. Through every mile, my heart has always remained at home with you. “Happy 66th birthday, my darling Oluremi. I pray that God Almighty will grant you many more years in good health and joy. May the years ahead bring you the same comfort and happiness you have so freely given to me and many others.” The post Tinubu to First Lady at 66: You’re my truest friend appeared first on Vanguard News .

Effurun attack: Keyamo fingers NDC thugs, vows action
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, has accused thugs loyal to the Nigeria Democratic Congress NDC of unleashing violence in his community in Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area of Delta State, vowing to petition the Inspector-General of Police IGP this week over the incident. Keyamo, in a post on his X handle, said he wanted “the world to see what the NDC’s thugs came to my community in Effurun, Uvwie LGA of Delta State, to do on Friday, 18th September, 2026.” He alleged that the thugs “wrecked havoc on billboards pasted everywhere by Tompolo’s door-to-door Campaign Organisation, entered people’s shops with dangerous weapons and looted the shops.” The minister lamented what he described as a double standard in public reactions to political violence, saying that “if it had been the other way round against the APC, the section of the bias Press and so-called human rights groups would have been screaming to high heavens, but since this happened, everywhere is mute.” Drawing a comparison with an earlier incident, Keyamo said, “this is the exact point I made when I openly condemned the blockade of Peter Obi’s entourage from entering Benue State. But what happened in Benue is nothing compared to this.” He described the situation as sickening, adding, “the double standards everywhere is sickening. The video is clear and the evidence is overwhelming. We have more evidence. The thugs were even accompanied by law-enforcement agents in their payroll.” The minister, who described himself as the foremost political leader in the community, said he would not let the matter slide, stating, “I have warned everyone not to resort to self-help.” He announced plans to escalate the matter to the police, saying, “I will be submitting a petition to the Inspector General of Police this week to thoroughly investigate this incident and bring all those found wanting to book (even against APC leaders, if anyone crossed the line).” Keyamo also called for disciplinary action against law enforcement agents allegedly complicit in the incident, adding, “disciplinary action should also be taken against those law-enforcement agents in their midst that condoned the looting and destruction of properties.” Keyamo further signalled a firmer resolve going forward, declaring, “some of us are now ready for the long haul!” The post Effurun attack: Keyamo fingers NDC thugs, vows action appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Kindia/Labota : un accident fait quatre morts et dix blessés
items.description: Vingt-quatre heures après l’accident de Friguiagbé, qui a causé trois morts, un nouvel accident de la circulation s’est produit ce dimanche 20 septembre 2026 à Labota, dans la sous-préfecture de Mambia, sur la route nationale Conakry–Kindia. Le bilan provisoire fait état de quatre morts (deux femmes et deux hommes) et de dix blessés (six femmes, trois hommes et un garçon), selon l’hôpital régional Alpha Oumar Diallo de Kindia. D’après les premières informations, la collision a impliqué un camion-remorque venant de Kindia et un véhicule de transport en commun en provenance de Conakry. Dr Moussa Camara, chargé de communication de l’hôpital, a indiqué : « Nous avons reçu 14 victimes, dont quatre corps et dix blessés. Les blessés présentent des traumatismes de gravité variable. Certains pourraient être transférés vers des structures hospitalières de Conakry. » Les corps des victimes ont été déposés à la morgue de l’hôpital, tandis que les blessés ont été pris en charge aux urgences. Les circonstances exactes de l’accident restent à déterminer. Mohamed L’article Kindia/Labota : un accident fait quatre morts et dix blessés est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Twelve Tribes of Israel Ghana to mark 40 years with anniversary celebration
items.description: The Twelve Tribes of Israel Ghana Chapter will mark its 40th anniversary with a celebration at the Arts Centre, Accra, on Saturday, 6 December 2026. The milestone event will feature a powerful lineup of international and Ghanaian reggae and highlife artistes, alongside community-focused activities designed to honour Rastafari’s contributions to national development over four decades. The anniversary concert will feature acclaimed international reggae voices including Micah Shemaiah, Patrick Junior and Mariam Simone, who will share the stage with home-grown talents such as Aklerh, Ras Caleb Appiah Levi, Nii Darko Positive D, Natty Gad and other special guests. The event will feature an evening of conscious music, cultural expression and unity in celebration of TTI Ghana’s enduring legacy. In keeping with its commitment to social responsibility, the 40th anniversary celebrations will extend beyond the concert hall. Activities lined up for the milestone include a donation to Nsawam Prisons to support rehabilitation and welfare initiatives, as well as a community soccer challenge to engage the youth in the community and foster unity through sport. There will also be a visit to the Kwame Nkrumah Memorial Park and other places of historical interest to reflect on Ghana’s leadership in Pan-Africanism and justice. These activities underscore TTI Ghana’s dedication to community development, youth empowerment and the preservation of cultural heritage. Speaking on the significance of the anniversary, Ahuma Bosco Ocansey, Overseer of the Twelve Tribes of Israel Ghana, stated, “The celebration is to herald what Rastafari has contributed to national development.” He cited President John Dramani Mahama’s recent statement at the United Nations, where the President described slavery as “the gravest crime against humanity”, as a reflection of the values and advocacy work TTI has championed over the last 40 years. The Twelve Tribes of Israel Ghana Chapter is a faith-based and cultural organisation rooted in Rastafari principles. For four decades, TTI Ghana has promoted spiritual growth, social justice, community service and the preservation of African heritage through music, education and outreach initiatives since its establishment in La in 1986.

items.title: U-20 Women’s World Cup: Semi-final fixtures confirmed
items.description: The semi-final line-up for the 2026 FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland has been confirmed following the completion of the quarter-final fixtures. Four teams — Italy, Spain, Colombia and North Korea — will compete for places in the final of the tournament. Colombia secured the final semi-final spot on Sunday after edging Nigeria 1-0 in a closely contested quarter-final. The South American side held on to its narrow advantage to end Nigeria’s campaign and book a place among the last four. North Korea also advanced after defeating Canada 2-0 in their quarter-final encounter. The two teams joined Spain and Italy, who had already secured their semi-final places following victories in Saturday’s quarter-final matches. The semi-final action will begin on Wednesday, with Spain taking on Italy in the first encounter. The second semi-final will see Colombia face North Korea, with both sides now two wins away from lifting the U-20 Women’s World Cup trophy. items.title: Kissidougou : à Tambassadou, 11 tables-bancs pour toute une école, le difficile chemin des enfants vers le savoir
items.description: À l’approche de la rentrée scolaire, certaines écoles de l’intérieur du pays continuent de faire face à d’importantes difficultés. À Tambassadou, district relevant de la sous-préfecture de Bardou, dans la préfecture de Kissidougou, l’école primaire publique Saint Albert illustre les réalités auxquelles sont confrontés de nombreux enfants en milieu rural. Située à 47 kilomètres de Kissidougou et à 7 kilomètres de Bardou, cette localité reste difficile d’accès. Les véhicules peinent à y parvenir, notamment en raison de l’absence de ponts sur certains passages. Seules les motos permettent véritablement de rallier le village. Pour les enfants, le parcours vers l’école constitue déjà une épreuve. Certains parcourent plusieurs kilomètres à pied chaque matin, parfois sous le soleil ou sous de fortes pluies, pour rejoindre les salles de classe. Créée en 2007 grâce à l’engagement de la communauté locale, l’école Saint Albert porte le nom d’Albert Tyéré Camara, présenté comme l’un des initiateurs du projet. « Cette école a été créée en 2007, et ça aussi par la bravoure de la communauté elle-même », explique Louis Mory Camara, professeur de chimie et ressortissant de Tambassadou. Deux salles pour six niveaux L’établissement ne dispose que de deux salles de classe pour accueillir les élèves de la première à la sixième année. Une situation qui contraint les enseignants à fonctionner en classes multigrades. « Les salles de classe qui sont fonctionnelles, il y en a deux. Et c’est multigrade aussi. Dans chaque salle, il y a deux promotions », témoigne Louis Mory Camara. À cette insuffisance s’ajoute le manque criant de mobilier. L’école ne compte que onze tables-bancs pour les élèves des deux groupes pédagogiques. Il arrive ainsi que cinq, voire six enfants, soient contraints de partager une même table-banc. « Il n’y a que onze tables-bancs pour ces deux groupes pédagogiques », précise-t-il. Le matériel pédagogique est également limité. Un petit tableau en bois figure parmi les rares équipements disponibles. Dans la cour, l’absence de clôture permet aux animaux de pénétrer librement dans l’enceinte scolaire. Des bœufs viennent notamment s’y abriter, laissant leurs déjections aux abords des salles. Même le bureau du directeur est utilisé comme espace de stockage, notamment pour conserver du bois mort apporté par certains élèves. Deux enseignants pour faire fonctionner l’école L’encadrement repose principalement sur deux enseignants titulaires, dont l’un assure également les fonctions de directeur. « L’école, pratiquement, on a deux titulaires. Donc ces deux titulaires sont ceux qui se débrouillent ici », explique Louis Mory Camara. Des enseignants contractuels viennent parfois renforcer l’équipe, mais leur prise en charge constitue une difficulté supplémentaire pour cette communauté essentiellement agricole. « Cette communauté qui est là ne se nourrit qu’à partir de l’agriculture. Donc s’il n’y a pas d’autre soutien, ça devient très, très difficile », souligne-t-il. L’école accueille des enfants de cinq villages : Tambassadou, Daadouto, Masamadou, Koleidou et Félembè. Cette année, 18 candidats ont été présentés à l’examen d’entrée en 7ᵉ année. Mais pour ceux qui réussissent, un autre obstacle les attend : poursuivre leurs études à Bardou, située à sept kilomètres. « Ces enfants viennent à pied chaque matin et rencontrent ces petits calvaires. Mais mieux vaut ici que de partir encore parcourir sept kilomètres pour rejoindre la sous-préfecture », estime Louis Mory Camara. Un appel aux autorités Face à ces difficultés, le ressortissant de Tambassadou appelle les autorités à soutenir la communauté afin d’améliorer les conditions d’apprentissage. « Le message que moi je peux demander à l’autorité, c’est de venir en aide à cette communauté qui se bat jour pour jour pour donner le savoir à ces petits-enfants qui sont là, qui n’ont nulle part où aller », plaide-t-il. Il estime que les enfants des zones rurales ne doivent pas être laissés en marge de l’accès à l’éducation. À Tambassadou, malgré un bâtiment en banco, deux salles de classe, onze tables-bancs et un personnel limité, l’école Saint Albert continue donc de fonctionner. Derrière ces conditions précaires, enseignants, parents et élèves tentent de maintenir vivant un espoir : celui de donner aux enfants les moyens de construire leur avenir par le savoir. Christine Finda Kamano L’article Kissidougou : à Tambassadou, 11 tables-bancs pour toute une école, le difficile chemin des enfants vers le savoir est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

Fret décarboné : la GIZ apporte son expertise au Maroc
items.description: Une nouvelle expertise allemande vient nourrir au Maroc la réflexion sur la décarbonation du transport de marchandises. La Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) a lancé une étude consacrée aux « corridors verts » et à l’électrification du fret routier, avec pour objectif d’examiner les conditions nécessaires au développement d’un transport de marchandises moins carboné. Ce marché relève de la procédure allemande UVgO et porte précisément sur une « Study on Green Corridors and the Electrification of Freight Transport in Morocco ». La date limite de remise des offres est fixée au 9 octobre 2026. L’avis public ne précise à ce stade ni le montant du marché ni les axes susceptibles d’entrer dans le périmètre de l’étude. Le choix du fret inscrit cette expertise dans une problématique qui dépasse la seule mobilité individuelle. L’électrification des véhicules de transport de marchandises soulève en effet des questions qui touchent à la fois aux infrastructures, à l’énergie et à l’organisation des flux logistiques. Pour le Maroc, où les infrastructures portuaires, industrielles et routières occupent une place centrale dans les échanges, la décarbonation du fret s’inscrit ainsi dans une réflexion plus large sur la performance et la soutenabilité des chaînes logistiques. Du véhicule au corridor logistique L’intérêt de l’approche retenue par la GIZ réside dans le passage d’une logique centrée sur le véhicule à une réflexion portant sur l’ensemble d’un itinéraire de transport. Pour le fret, l’électrification ne dépend pas uniquement de l’autonomie des véhicules. Elle implique également les infrastructures de recharge, la disponibilité de l’électricité, les capacités du réseau, les temps d’immobilisation et les contraintes propres à l’exploitation des poids lourds. La notion de « corridor vert » renvoie ainsi à une approche plus large de la transition du transport de marchandises. Elle permet d’articuler les infrastructures et les besoins énergétiques avec les impératifs propres aux opérateurs de fret, pour lesquels la continuité du service, les délais d’acheminement et les coûts d’exploitation constituent des paramètres déterminants. Pour le Maroc, cette problématique intervient dans un contexte où le transport occupe une place importante dans la consommation énergétique et les émissions de carbone. Selon la GIZ, le secteur représente près de 30 % des émissions marocaines de CO₂ et environ 38 % de la consommation finale d’énergie. L’organisme relève également que le parc de véhicules en circulation a plus que doublé entre 2006 et 2018, sous l’effet notamment de l’urbanisation et de la progression du trafic routier. Ces données donnent une dimension particulière à l’étude commandée par la coopération allemande. La réduction de l’empreinte carbone du transport ne concerne pas uniquement les déplacements individuels ou la mobilité urbaine. Elle s’étend également aux flux professionnels de marchandises, directement liés aux chaînes d’approvisionnement, aux échanges commerciaux et à l’activité des différents pôles économiques du Royaume. Une coopération allemande déjà engagée La nouvelle étude s’inscrit par ailleurs dans une coopération déjà active sur les questions de mobilité durable et de transition énergétique au Maroc. Depuis août 2022, la GIZ met en œuvre un programme consacré à la mobilité alimentée par les énergies renouvelables, en partenariat avec le ministère marocain de la Transition énergétique et du Développement durable. Financé par le ministère fédéral allemand de la Coopération économique et du Développement (BMZ), ce programme est prévu jusqu’au 31 juillet 2027 et représente un volume de 6 millions d’euros. Les travaux engagés dans ce cadre portent notamment sur l’intégration des différents modes de transport, l’électromobilité, la numérisation et l’accessibilité de la mobilité. Agadir figure notamment parmi les territoires pilotes, avec des travaux consacrés aux politiques et aux plans locaux de mobilité. L’appel d’offres publié récemment ajoute donc une composante spécifiquement consacrée au transport de marchandises à cette coopération. Son intitulé associe deux dimensions complémentaires : le développement de corridors verts et l’électrification du fret. Cette orientation élargit le champ des enjeux de mobilité durable à un segment dont les contraintes techniques et économiques sont sensiblement différentes de celles des véhicules particuliers. Elle place notamment la question des infrastructures énergétiques au centre de la réflexion. L’électricité au cœur de l’équation Pour le transport lourd, l’électrification pose des contraintes spécifiques. Les besoins de puissance, la localisation des installations de recharge, la durée des arrêts, l’autonomie des véhicules et la capacité du réseau électrique deviennent des paramètres directement liés à la faisabilité des solutions envisagées. Cette dimension explique l’association, dans l’intitulé même du marché, entre électrification et corridors. La réflexion ne porte pas seulement sur la technologie embarquée dans les véhicules, mais sur l’environnement énergétique et infrastructurel permettant leur exploitation sur des itinéraires de fret. Pour le Maroc, cet enjeu rejoint également la transformation du système électrique. Le Royaume vise une part de 52 % d’énergies renouvelables dans son bouquet électrique à l’horizon 2030. L’électrification du transport de marchandises peut dès lors être examinée à l’intersection de deux trajectoires : la réduction de l’utilisation des carburants fossiles dans les transports et l’augmentation de la production d’électricité issue de sources renouvelables. items.title: Maroc : quels enjeux pour les élections législatives ?
items.description: Le Maroc renouvelle les 395 sièges de sa Chambre des représentants lors des élections législatives du 23 septembre. Le scrutin se déroule dans un cadre électoral réformé, avec notamment de nouvelles dispositions concernant les candidatures, le financement politique et la représentation des femmes et des jeunes. Mais au-delà des règles du scrutin, quelles sont les attentes des Marocains ? Pouvoir d’achat, emploi, éducation, santé : les partis politiques peuvent-ils répondre aux préoccupations de la population et restaurer la confiance dans la représentation politique ? Décryptage avec Nadia Hachimi Alaoui dans le Journal de l’Afrique.

items.title: Oshiomhole demands independent probe into miners’ deaths
items.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — Chairman of the Senate Committee on Interior, Senator Adams Oshiomhole, has called for a thorough, transparent and independent investigation into the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, NSCDC, in Niger State. Oshiomhole, who represents Edo North Senatorial District, said the investigation should establish the circumstances surrounding the deaths, including the conditions under which the detainees were held, the medical attention provided to them and those who survived, as well as the actual cause of death. In a statement issued by his office on Sunday, the former Edo State governor said the fact that the deceased were arrested on allegations of illegal mining did not remove their right to humane treatment. He said every person, regardless of the offence for which he or she was accused, deserved to be treated with dignity, respect and in accordance with the law. Oshiomhole described the incident as tragic and urged relevant authorities to allow ongoing investigations to establish the precise circumstances surrounding the deaths. He also called for an immediate assessment of detention and correctional facilities across the country to ensure that they meet acceptable standards of safety, sanitation, ventilation and human dignity. The senator commiserated with the families, relatives and communities of the 37 deceased miners, praying for strength for them to bear the loss. He also prayed for the speedy recovery of those who survived the incident and are receiving medical attention. Oshiomhole commended Niger State Governor, Mohammed Umaru Bago; Minister of Interior, Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo; and the Commandant-General of the NSCDC, Professor Ahmed Abubakar Audi, for what he described as their prompt response to the crisis and steps taken to commence investigations. He urged Nigerians to remain calm while the authorities establish the facts surrounding the incident. The senator stressed that accountability, justice and respect for human dignity must remain central to the administration of the country’s detention and security system. The post Oshiomhole demands independent probe into miners’ deaths appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GPL 2026/27: Hearts held by Bechem as Kotoko, Samartex share spoils
items.description: Hearts of Oak dropped points for the first time this season after a goalless draw with Bechem United, while Asante Kotoko and Samartex shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw in the Ghana Premier League on Sunday. The Phobians struggled to break down a disciplined Bechem defence at the University of Ghana Stadium, ending their winning run after victories over Bibiani Gold Stars and Berekum Chelsea. The result extended Hearts’ unbeaten start to three matches and kept them top of the table. At the Nsenkyire Sports Arena, Kotoko goalkeeper Ibrahim Danlad saved a penalty in the 66th minute before former Samartex striker Emmanuel Mamah headed the visitors into the lead nine minutes later. Christian Agyenim Boateng equalised eight minutes later to preserve Samartex’s unbeaten home record. Samartex moved into second place, level on points with Hearts, while Kotoko remained fourth with five points after three matches, still without an away win. Hearts travel to face Karela United, while Bechem host Dreams FC. Kotoko welcome Aduana FC, with Samartex visiting Swedru All Blacks. items.title: Aleema detained under MPO in Lahore ahead of PTI's Sept 27 protest
items.description: PTI said on Sunday that ex-prime minister and party founder Imran Khan’s sister, Aleema Khan, had been detained by authorities, after the office of Lahore’s deputy commissioner (DC) ordered her detention or arrest for 30 days. The development takes place amid reports of a crackdown on the PTI ahead of its September 27 countrywide protest and march to Islamabad, which the party has called to demand Imran’s release from jail and mobilise people for the supremacy of the Constitution. The September 20 order, a copy of which is available with Dawn , said DC Muhammad Ali Ijaz had ordered the detention or arrest of Aleema and a man named Muhammad Ameer under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 (MPO). The MPO ordinance allows the authorities to order detention and restrict judicial review of such orders. “Their custody shall be placed under the superintendent, Central Jail, Kot Lakhpat, Lahore. They shall be at liberty to make a representation to the provincial government against this order,” the document read. Police sources confirmed to Dawn that Aleema had been taken to the Kot Lakhpat jail. Following the arrest, Aleema’s sister Noreen Niazi addressed a press conference in Lahore, flanked by her sister’s counsel Advocate Mudassir Umar. Noreen claimed Aleema was “picked up” along with her driver after she left her residence on Saturday and they later learnt that Aleema’s vehicle was parked at a police station. Meanwhile, the lawyer said they had yet to receive official confirmation of her arrest. Aleema’s son Shahrez Khan, in a post on X, alleged his mother “was abducted after leaving home this morning”. “Our family has had no contact or news of her whereabouts,” he wrote, clarifying that Aleema was on bail in all cases against her in Lahore. “We demand the government immediately disclose her whereabouts and ensure her safe return,” Shahrez wrote. The DC’s order cited a letter by the Lahore capital city police officer. It said the letter referred to police reports that said Aleema and Ameer “are prejudicial to the public safety and maintenance of public order”. According to the order, the reports also mentioned that the two had been involved in roadblocks and protests on May 9, 2023, when PTI supporters and workers took to the streets against Imran’s arrest. “They motivated the workers to damage public and government property. Moreover, they are again mobilising the workers through social media and public meetings to create law and order situation, raising/chanting objectionable slogans amongst the general public against the government/institution in order to provoke and incite them,” the order read. It said multiple cases had been registered against the two, declaring them “potential dangers to public peace and tranquillity”. According to the order, the Civil Lines Division superintendent of police and district intelligence branch in-charge recommended their detention under the MPO for a 30-day period “in order to keep the law and order situation in the city intact”. Later in the day, PTI Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram claimed that MNAs Sanaullah Mastikhel , Ahsan Jamal Khan and Mian Ghous had been taken into custody. According to him, Jamal was detained “in front of the National Assembly”. In his X posts, Akram also said that Noreen’s daughter and son-in-law were released after brief detention in Lahore. Ministers slam MNA Junaid Akbar’s remarks Meanwhile, PTI MNA Junaid Akbar defended his remarks regarding his party’s upcoming march, wherein he said that they would turn Islamabad into Somnath, a historic Indian temple, and “would keep on lifting corpses and new people would also come”. Akbar’s clarification came after government representatives, including Defence Minister Khawaja Asif and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, criticised his comments. The PTI leader contended that his statements were given “a wrong spin” by certain journalists and individuals. “We were peaceful, we are peaceful, and we will remain peaceful. I used the reference to Somnath to indicate returning repeatedly,” he said in a post on X. “Whoever is not peaceful will not be a soldier of Imran Khan,” the lawmaker added, urging party workers to “keep an eye on those people who try to harm the movement”. “Imran Khan has always said that this country is also mine, this army is also mine.” “Their language reveals just how Pakistani they are. And to what extremes they can go for the sake of seizing power. And what a lesson Imran Khan has taught them,” Asif said on X, referring to Akbar’s remarks. “These people were enemies of peace, progress, and Pakistan yesterday; they are so today; and they will remain so tomorrow as well,” the minister said. Meanwhile, Tarar said: “This shows their intention to create chaos and destruction. “Their call for protest is illegal and we will not allow them to block roads and disrupt people’s lives.” Speaking to Geo News on Akbar’s remarks, Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry warned that there would be no tolerance for “anything that was unlawful, a danger to people’s lives or property, or that affected the routine life”. He recalled previous protests by PTI that had turned violent, such as the May 9 riots of 2023 and the Nov 26, 2024 clashes in Islamabad. The state minister asserted that rights guaranteed under the Constitution did not allow one to carry out an “attack”. “If you are a peaceful citizen, come to Islamabad […] we will definitely provide you protection and every kind of facility, but if you come as terrorists, then you will not return,” the PML-N leader said. ‘Pressure’ Describing the development as part of “pressure” ahead of the September 27 protest, Noreen said the date would be a “historic day” in what she described as a movement for Imran’s release. “We are all part of this movement,” she told reporters, urging PTI supporters not to be afraid despite what she alleged was a crackdown involving raids on homes. She called on people to come out “for their country and Imran Khan”, alleging that his brother was being kept in custody unjustly and was not receiving proper medical treatment. “If they think that by arresting Aleema Khan we will be frightened, they are mistaken,” she declared. Advocate Umar noted an MPO(3) order had been circulating on social media and purportedly named Aleema and Ameer. However, he said, the government had not yet officially acknowledged Aleema’s detention. “We are working out a legal course of action against the arrest. The government should own the arrest so that we can seek legal remedy,” the lawyer said. He claimed that police had already informed a court that Aleema was not involved in the Jinnah House attack case pertaining to the May 9 riots. The lawyer further claimed that the MPO order appeared to have been issued after Aleema was taken into custody, and alleged that her arrest was linked to her being the sister of Imran Khan. Soon after reports emerged of Aleema’s arrest, PTI Chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan wrote on X: “We have clarified that our protest will be peaceful. Our objective is to peacefully struggle for the fulfilment of our constitutional and political demands; we don’t want any kind of clash or violence. “Arresting Aleema Khan sahiba under the MPO in this situation is tantamount to fuelling violence and tension. We strongly condemn it.” He called for an end to all such actions and demanded Aleema’s immediate release. The party would soon present its strategy against such actions, he said. Earlier, the PTI posted on X that Aleema had been “abducted” in Lahore from outside her home by the authorities. In another statement, the party termed the action a “cowardly and deliberate attempt to worsen the situation”. “Who is responsible for shameful news coming out of Pakistan almost every day now?” PTI wrote in yet another post sharing a Reuters report on the arrest. PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram demanded that Aleema be presented in court immediately. “A sister is being punished for speaking up for her brother,” Akram alleged on X. Imran’s son Kasim Khan, who has recently been speaking to international media about his father’s incarceration, wrote on X: “First they imprisoned my father. Now they are coming after his family.” Assailing the government, he said, “The world cannot keep looking away from what is happening in Pakistan.” Opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) also condemned the arrest in a statement, saying the move was tantamount to crossing all limits of “state oppression and political revenge. “The TTAP strongly condemns this step by the government, especially the Punjab government. This action exposes the Punjab government’s current oppressive system,” it added. The opposition alliance said Aleema’s arrest would not be tolerated and demanded her immediate release. “The Punjab government must realise that oppression, arrests and revengeful acts cannot resolve political differences,” the TTAP said, reiterating its demand for Aleema’s release, as well as that of other “political prisoners”. Detentions ahead of protest Aleema’s arrest follows a string of reported actions against the PTI in Punjab ahead of its September 27 protest. District authorities had also issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under MPO a week ago, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh. Similar reports have come from Islamabad, where the PTI plans to march on the protest day. However, the government has vowed to stop the march, and the Islamabad High Court (IHC) has ruled that no political party or its leadership has the “lawful right to occupy public roads, highways, interchanges, toll plazas and buildings in Islamabad”. On Saturday, the capital police took into custody four PTI activists and workers. A police officer told Dawn the activists were arrested under separate charges on a complaint lodged by a sub-inspector. The police got information that the PTI workers were holding a meeting in connection with the planned protest at a property dealer’s office in the area of E-16. Subsequently, a police team was constituted for the raid and arrests. The police claimed that the workers tortured the police team when they raided the meeting venue, besides tearing their uniforms and taking them hostage. On Thursday, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja said he was “released” after being briefly detained, with the party claiming he was held by Islamabad police. Officers in the police and capital administration also said they have started preparations to counter the PTI’s countrywide protest. Authorities have placed hundreds of containers at the city’s entry points as the administration braces for protests.

items.title: My Story (Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako)
items.description: Dear Angel, As you begin your secondary school education, I want you to always keep this in mind: Education can make a difference in your life. I come from a poor background. Growing up in a large but poor family, life was very difficult. I worked hard to pass my middle school (JHS) exams and was duly qualified to go to secondary school (SHS). During our days, there were three school terms per academic year. I could not begin First Term with the other students, because my parents could not afford the basics I needed plus school fees, even as a day student. So, I missed First Term. When I finally entered Form One during the Second Term, I had a lot of work to do to catch up. Copying all the notes for all the subjects from my new classmates, trying to learn everything they had studied for a whole term while at the same time managing to cope with Second Term lessons that were in many instances supposed to build upon First Term lessons, was very difficult. In one Twi class, the Teacher once gave me a hard knock on the head because I had made a mistake. He said he had corrected the class on that very subject matter several times during the First Term. He did not even care to know that I was not present in his class during the First Term. I wept, but I had no choice than to endure the pain and continue to learn. I passed my O-Level exams and came to Accra to pursue my A-Levels and then entered the University of Ghana Business School (then called School of Administration). Throughout my O-Level studies, life was extremely difficult. At one point, I actually wanted to drop out of school. One thing that kept me going was that the efforts I put into learning always paid off during exams, and that was my encouragement. I had support from some generous classmates who came from relatively wealthy homes, to whom I remain eternally grateful. But there were others who always made me feel the poverty I had to deal with. I remember one person in particular who once asked me, “why are you so poor”? In all of this, my only solace was to study hard. At the University of Ghana, my only source of income was the student loan, which was never enough to cover academic materials and personal needs. There were nights I went hungry, but still had to study. After first degree, I got a job right after school. Several years later, I decided to go and do my second degree (MBA) at the University of Leicester, in England. I went there without a scholarship and was required to pay the full fees for the course. To support myself, I had to work at night, doing whatever jobs I could find, while I went for lectures during the day. I sometimes worked in factories processing food; and I sometimes worked as a security officer at supermarkets. In all this, my only goal was to get education, which I believed would make a difference in my life. Today, while I’m not a rich person, I’m also not a poor person. I am able to support myself, my immediate family, my aged mother, and other persons as and when I need to. When I look back at my life’s journey, from a poor secondary school student to who I am today, the only difference is EDUCATION. My only advice to you as you begin SHS is, focus on your studies. Don’t get distracted by social media and friends. The only thing that can change your life, the life of your mom who is working hard to support you and the life of your little sister, is education. Keep this in mind and give yourself the chance to succeed by making good use of this opportunity of secondary education. This is my personal experience and I hope my story will help you. Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako September 19, 2026.

items.title: Burkina/Entrepreneuriat : Yamdicré Academy forme une trentaine de jeunes en saponification
items.description: Burkina/Entrepreneuriat : Yamdicré Academy forme une trentaine de jeunes en saponification Ouagadougou, 19 septembre 2026 (AIB)-La structure Yamdicré Academy a organisé, du 18 au 19 septembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, une formation gratuite en saponification au profit d'une trentaine de jeunes, sous le thème « Formation, jeunesse et entrepreneuriat ». « L'initiative vise à permettre au jeune d'acquérir des compétences pratiques dans différents métiers », a déclaré le promoteur de Yamdicré Academy, par ailleurs formateur, Wendkuni Barnabas Ouédraogo. Selon lui, « cette initiative s'inscrit dans une démarche de conscientisation de la jeunesse et de promotion de l'entrepreneuriat ». « Durant les deux jours de formation, les participants ont appris la fabrication du savon de lessive, du savon liquide, du kabakourou, de l'eau de Javel, du shampooing », a affirmé Wendkuni Barnabas Ouédraogo. « La fabrication de la pommade de beauté, la pommade mentholée et également des conseils pour être utile à la société », a-t-il ajouté. M. Ouédraogo a exhorté les bénéficiaires à mettre en pratique les connaissances acquises. « Nous sommes les dignes fils de ce pays et nous avons le devoir de nous sacrifier pour la génération future ». Pour sa part, la bénéficiaire Asséta Konkobo a salué l'initiative portée par la structure Yamdicré Academy. Elle a laissé entendre que « grâce à cette formation, j'aurai désormais une source de revenus à travers la production du savon liquide ». De son côté, Fatoumata Ouédraogo s'est engagée à partager les connaissances acquises au cours de la formation afin d'en faire bénéficier sa communauté. Née en janvier 2025, Yamdicré Academy œuvre pour la formation de la jeunesse, la promotion de l'entrepreneuriat et le développement personnel. Agence d'Information du Burkina FT/ata

items.title: We expect growth rate to re-accelerate in second-half of 2026 – IC Insights
items.description: Ghana’s Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth will re-accelerate in the second-half of 2026. This is coming after it eased to 6.0% year-on-year in quarter 2026, reflecting softer non-oil activity and moderation in agriculture, gold and public services. According to IC Securities, it remains confident about continued recovery in oil & gas output into the second-half of 2026 as Tullow Oil PLC’s management guidance indicates that new wells came on stream in July and August 2026, with initial production rates being in line with expectations. “We tip ICT [Information, Communication and Technology] to remain the growth anchor for Services while transports & storage, financial & insurance activities as well as trades provide further tailwind. We expect a boost in economic activity in 4Q2026 [quarter 4 2026] as the annual yuletide activities revive house final consumption expenditure”. It therefore retains its full-year 2026 overall real GDP growth forecast at 6.4% ± 0.5 percentage points. Services Sector The Services sector growth accelerated to 8.0% year-on-year from 7.1% in the first quarter of 2026, but the pace remains below the 9.5% recorded in like period of 2025. This retains the services sector as Ghana’s growth engine, contributing 57.6% of the overall growth in quarter 2 2026. Information and communication sub-sector extended its remarkable growth to 30.9% year-on-year versus 25.2% in quarter one 2026 and 21.3% in the second quarter of 2025, anchoring the services sector. Industry Sector Industry growth eased to 4.3% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026 compared to the early-year pace of 6.9% in the first quarter of 2026, but represented an acceleration from the 2.4% modest growth in the corresponding quarter of 2025. “We note a sharp slowdown in the growth rate for Mining & Quarrying to 2.6% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026 compared to 10.7% in first quarter of 2026, although the 2Q2026 momentum represents a rebound from 1.8% contraction a year earlier”, IC Insights stated. Agriculture Sector Agriculture growth slowed to 3.9% year-on-year from 7.1% a year earlier and a tad below the 4.0% recorded in quarter one 2026. This dragged down by deep contraction in fishing (-24.7%) which posted the third consecutive contraction. Although the cocoa sector grew faster in the second quarter of 2026 by 5.2% year-on-year, the latest print represents a 900-basis points slowdown in growth compared to quarter 2 2025. “We attribute this partly to high base effect from last year’s rebound and expect the sector to benefit from the authorities’ efforts to secure domestic financing for cocoa purchases and improve the financing architecture for 2026/27 crop season”, IC Insights mentioned. It however said that the usual crop harvest in the third quarter of 2026 should also lift crops and the broader agricultural sector growth towards year-end

items.title: Affacturage : la Banque d’Algérie fixe 7 conditions d’éligibilité
items.description: La Banque d’Algérie a promulgué un règlement fixant des règles strictes pour l’activité d’affacturage par les banques et les établissements financiers. L’article 2 du règlement publié ce dimanche 20 au Journal officiel définit l’affacturage ou factoring comme une « opération par laquelle l’adhérent transfère, dans le cadre d’une convention écrite, avec effet subrogatoire, ses créances commerciales sur ses clients, à une banque ou un établissement financier qui, moyennant rémunération, lui règle ferme le montant intégral de la créance transférée en supportant le risque de non remboursement. Sept conditions à satisfaire pour être éligibles à l’affacturage La Banque d’Algérie fixe sept critères pour être éligibles aux opérations d’affacturage. Il s’agit de : 1-Etre certaines, liquides et déterminées dans leur montant, et ne pas faire l’objet de contestation de la part du débiteur ; 2-Etre assorties d’une échéance de paiement d’un délai inférieur à six mois, à compter de la date de facturation ; 3- Ne pas être éteintes, en tout ou en partie, par paiement, par compensation avec des dettes vis-à-vis du débiteur ou par tout autre mode légal d’extinction des obligations ; 4-Être librement transmissibles et ne faire l'objet d'aucune interdiction légale, réglementaire ou contractuelle de transfert des droits de créance opposables au factor ; 5- Ne pas être grevées, à la date du transfert, d’une cession, d’un nantissement ou de toute autre sûreté ou charge susceptible d’affecter les droits du factor ; 6- Ne pas porter sur un débiteur en situation de cessation des paiements, de redressement judiciaire, de liquidation des biens ou toute situation similaire ; 7-Ne pas faire l'objet, à la date de transfert, d'une prorogation d'échéance, pour tout ou partie de leur montant, sous quelque forme que ce soit. En plus, la Banque d’Algérie interdit tout contrat d’affacturage ayant pour objet le « financement de créances ayant déjà fait l’objet d’un financement en vertu d’un autre contrat d’affacturage. » L’article Affacturage : la Banque d'Algérie fixe 7 conditions d'éligibilité est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: ZLECAf, fintech et énergies vertes : Le chef de l'ONU met en avant le potentiel économique africain
items.description: L’Afrique s’affirme de plus en plus comme un pôle majeur d’investissement et de croissance de l’économie mondiale, portée par l’essor de sa main-d’œuvre, l’abondance de ses ressources naturelles et son potentiel dans les énergies renouvelables, a affirmé dimanche le Secrétaire général des Nations unies, António Guterres. Intervenant à l’ouverture de la cinquième édition du forum “Unstoppable Africa”, M. Guterres a indiqué que l’Afrique, un marché estimé à 3.000 milliards de dollars, dispose de 30 % des ressources minérales mondiales et de 60 % du potentiel solaire de la planète. Cette dynamique traduit un changement de paradigme, passant de “faire des affaires en Afrique” à “faire des affaires avec l’Afrique”, a-t-il relevé, appelant à approfondir les investissements et à bâtir des partenariats économiques davantage fondés sur la création de valeur locale. Les perspectives sont particulièrement prometteuses dans les secteurs des énergies propres et des nouvelles technologies, a souligné le chef de l’ONU, notant que cette transformation touche également les domaines de la finance et des industries culturelles. La fintech constitue, dans ce sens, le “principal secteur africain en matière d’attraction des capitaux d’investissement”, a-t-il relevé, alors que les échanges dans le cadre de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf) devraient atteindre 230 milliards de dollars cette année. Face aux tensions commerciales actuelles, a poursuivi le chef de l’ONU, l’Afrique est appelée à transformer ces défis en opportunités, en passant d’économies principalement tournées vers l’exportation de matières premières à des modèles capables de retenir et d’accroître davantage la valeur ajoutée sur le continent. M. Guterres a, dans ce contexte, réitéré son appel à une réforme de l’architecture financière internationale afin de mieux répondre aux besoins des pays en développement, ainsi qu’à davantage de financements climatiques et d’investissements en faveur des jeunes et des femmes. Placée sous le thème “Unstoppable Africa 2026 : Stimuler les entreprises, développer les économies, façonner l'avenir”, cette rencontre, qui réunit plus de 2 000 chefs d’entreprise, innovateurs et investisseurs du monde entier, met l'accent sur la conclusion d'accords et le lancement de véhicules d'investissement à même de conserver la valeur sur le continent. items.title: The ungodliness and unrighteousness underlying the National Cathedral mess!
items.description: 1. When former President Akufo-Addo claimed that he had made a personal pledge to God to build the National Cathedral if God helped him to win the election to become President, did anybody ask him the size of the cathedral he promised to God? 2. If President Akufo-Addo indeed made what should have been a spiritual pledge, did he also promise God and did God insist that the cathedral should be one that would cost $400 million? 3. If President Akufo-Addo had even read the bible, would he not have known that God does not dwell in temples? 4. Could President Akufo-Addo not have converted his Nima residence into a cathedral or built a 100-seater cathedral or whatever at Kyebi to fulfil his personal pledge to God without wasting national resources? 5. Was the pledge he made to God about a cathedral or the size of the cathedral? 6. Did he tell God that he was going to use resources that did not belong to him to fulfil his personal pledge? And God accepted that pledge and urged President Akufo-Addo to go ahead and fulfil it? 7. Which God will accept for you to waste the resources of the State to fulfil your personal pledge or sacrifice? 8. Which scriptural text provides any spiritual foundation to support such ungodly and unrighteous dissipation of resources that should be spent to better the lives of the very poor people that Nana Akufo-Addo had promised to serve if elected President? 9. Could the lives of the poor people in Nima where President Akufo-Addo lives not be made better with the $100 million wasted to dig that pit? 10. And the clergy jumped on this deception hook, line and sinker to help waste public resources, in the name of God? Kwaku Antwi-Boasiako, Accra September 19, 2026

JI launches protest march towards Islamabad against petroleum levy
items.description: Jamaat-i-Islami launched its protest march towards Islamabad on Sunday, with party chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman warning that if the government failed to abolish the petroleum levy, the protest could turn into one to oust the government. In the morning, Naeem made a speech at Karachi’s Cantonment Station before departing for Islamabad by train. After addressing supporters in Hyderabad during his journey, Naeem held a rally upon reaching Sukkur at night. Addressing the Sukkur gathering, the JI chief accused the PPP-led Sindh government of creating obstacles throughout the day for its supporters, including people coming from Shikarpur and Balochistan. “We tell the Sindh government that this method is not correct,” he said. In his Karachi speech, the party chief said that a road caravan had also departed for the federal capital in addition to the “train march”. He added that the rally would pass through Hyderabad, Landhi, Nawabshah, Rohri and Sukkur, adding that “we will invite our sisters to join us once we reach [Islamabad]”. Rehman said the purpose of the march was to help relieve the burden on the least privileged. “Instead of providing relief to the people, the government has decided that it would make the nation pay for its bad governance,” he added. “We demand that the levy extortion should end. Petrol prices would then reduce quickly and reach around Rs200 per litre. That’s when the economy could move forward.” He said that the government had increased petrol prices more than any other state in the region. “The government wants to rob the common people in times of crisis,” Naeem claimed. The JI emir said voicing complaints on social media was pointless, urging supporters to step out of their houses to protest the injustice. “For the past 36-37 days, nationwide protests have been ongoing,” he said, adding that protests were currently under way in Hyderabad, Sukkur, Mirpurkhas, Larkana, Naushahro Feroze, Rawalpindi, Gujrat and various cities of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. “JI has mobilised entire Pakistan,” he said. “No hindrances can stop the protesters.” “When we reach Islamabad, it’s not guaranteed that the situation would remain under control,” Rehman warned. If the government tried to suppress the movement, the situation would get out of control, he said. The party posted on X that the protesters would depart for Multan on Monday. The JI has been holding nationwide protests against the fuel levy, which is more than Rs100 per litre. Address in Hyderabad As the JI’s convoy reached Hyderabad, the JI chief addressed party workers gathered at the Hyderabad Railway Station. He said the enthusiasm expressed by people at the station showed that JI’s movement against price hikes and recovery of petroleum levy had resonated with the public. He urged people to reach Islamabad and claimed that neither he nor the JI have any personal interest; rather, the matter concerned the people of Pakistan. Rehman said the march had turned into a huge revolutionary one. He said that people had been mobilised across Pakistan towards Islamabad, demanding the levy be withdrawn. On JI’s talks with the government, he said that while the party held negotiations, the federal government had nothing to offer to the people. “If you are under some compulsion and cannot do anything, then JI is under compulsion that it has to stand with people,” he said, adding that the party’s talks with the government were conditional upon whether the latter offered any relief. On Saturday, a government delegation, including PML-N leaders Rana Sanaullah, Ahsan Iqbal, and Salman Rafique, called on the JI leadership at its Mansoorah headquarters in Lahore, but the meeting failed to break the deadlock. During the talks, the government delegation asked the JI to postpone the long march in view of security threats. However, JI leader Liaquat Baloch said the long march would remain necessary until the levy imposed on the public was withdrawn. Talks between the JI and the government began on Sept 7. The party has been staging regular sit-ins in Lahore, Peshawar, Karachi and dozens of other locations across the country since August 16 to protest the levy. Meanwhile, PTI is also scheduled to stage its protest in the capital on Sept 27 for the release of Imran Khan, among other demands. It also turned down the government’s request to postpone the march, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas said a day earlier.

items.title: BURKINA : 15 bachelières distinguées au concours d’excellence scientifique « Hakili Mousso »
items.description: BURKINA-EXCELLENCE-SCIENTIFIQUE-FEMININE BURKINA : 15 bachelières distinguées au concours d'excellence scientifique « Hakili Mousso » Ouagadougou, 20 septembre 2026 (AIB)-Le Burkina Faso a célébré, samedi, l'excellence scientifique féminine à l'issue de la première édition du concours scientifique national « Hakili Mousso ». Au cours d'une cérémonie présidée par le Premier ministre, Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, représentant le Président du Faso, le Capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, les 15 meilleures bachelières en mathématiques, physique et chimie, ainsi que leurs enseignants référents, ont été distingués. Après les phases régionales, 84 candidates ont pris part à la cérémonie officielle de proclamation des résultats du concours national de détection des talents scientifiques féminins. Cinq prix ont été attribués dans chacune des trois disciplines retenues. Les récompenses comprennent des sommes allant de 500 000 à 2 millions de FCFA, des ordinateurs, des bourses d'études, ainsi qu'une prise en charge de la santé, de la restauration, du logement et du transport pendant la durée des études. Des motos, des bons de carburant et d'autres lots ont également été décernés. Les enseignants référents des lauréates ont, eux aussi, été récompensés. Ils repartent avec des villas, des ordinateurs, des motos et d'autres lots. « Les filles ont pleinement leur place dans les matières scientifiques », a déclaré le Premier ministre, appelant les jeunes filles à ne pas avoir peur de s'engager dans ces domaines. Il a également insisté sur le rôle des enseignants et des parents dans l'accompagnement des jeunes filles qui choisissent de s'orienter vers les filières scientifiques. Selon la ministre conseillère spéciale du Président du Faso, Floriane Zongo, les filles représentaient 36,7 % des effectifs des filières scientifiques en 2025-2026, contre 59,5 % dans les filières non scientifiques. À travers l'initiative présidentielle « Hakili Mousso », les autorités entendent renforcer l'intérêt des jeunes filles pour les disciplines scientifiques et technologiques, en vue de favoriser le développement des compétences nécessaires à la transformation technique et industrielle du Burkina Faso. La représentante des lauréates, Nicole Yaméogo, a salué cette initiative et exprimé, au nom de ses camarades, leur joie et leur détermination à poursuivre leurs efforts. « Grâce à Hakili Mousso, nous avons la conviction d'avoir un rôle crucial à jouer dans le développement et la souveraineté de notre patrie. Nous prenons l'engagement de demeurer d'excellentes ambassadrices de la science et de mettre nos compétences, notre vigueur et notre travail au service du Burkina Faso », a-t-elle déclaré. Agence d'Information du Burkina JT/ata

items.title: Gossas : le 3FPT mise sur la proximité pour rapprocher les jeunes de la formation
items.description: À Gossas, les 72 Heures de l’emploi et de la formation professionnelle prennent une dimension résolument pratique. Entre information, orientation et échanges directs, le 3FPT et la Direction de l’Emploi rapprochent les dispositifs publics des jeunes, des femmes et des porteurs de projets. Avec l’initiative « Une ASC, des métiers », le 3FPT entend également s’appuyer sur le mouvement associatif pour élargir l’accès à la formation et à l’insertion. À Gossas, la formation professionnelle est allée à la rencontre des populations. La première journée des 72 Heures de l’emploi et de la formation professionnelle, tenue samedi 19 septembre, a été marquée par une forte dimension de proximité. Dans les stands et les espaces d’échange, jeunes, femmes et porteurs de projets sont venus s’informer sur les opportunités de formation, les mécanismes de financement et les dispositifs d’accompagnement vers l’emploi. Au stand du Fonds de financement de la formation professionnelle et technique (3FPT), les échanges ont essentiellement porté sur les possibilités de financement de la formation professionnelle, les conditions d’accès et les démarches d’enrôlement. À quelques mètres, la Direction de l’Emploi présentait ses mécanismes d’orientation et d’accompagnement vers l’insertion. Cette présence de proximité répond à un enjeu essentiel : permettre aux populations de mieux connaître les dispositifs publics et, surtout, de savoir comment y accéder. Pour beaucoup de jeunes et de femmes, l’information constitue en effet la première étape avant la formation, la qualification ou l’insertion. Les ASC comme relais Cette dynamique s’est poursuivie dimanche avec la rencontre consacrée à l’initiative « Une ASC, des métiers ». Présidée par le Directeur général du 3FPT, Souleye Kane, la rencontre a réuni les responsables des mouvements de jeunesse, des représentants des ASC, des femmes et plusieurs acteurs locaux. À travers cette initiative, le 3FPT entend faire des associations sportives et culturelles un relais supplémentaire pour rapprocher les jeunes de la formation professionnelle. Le mouvement associatif, particulièrement présent dans les quartiers et les localités, apparaît ainsi comme un espace privilégié pour diffuser l’information et identifier les besoins en qualification. Le Directeur général a présenté les dispositifs d’accompagnement du 3FPT ainsi que les actions réalisées dans le département de Gossas entre 2021 et 2026. Il a également annoncé la mise en place d’un programme spécial destiné aux 107 associations sportives et culturelles (ASC) du département. La rencontre a également permis de recueillir les préoccupations exprimées par les jeunes et les femmes sur les questions de qualification et d’insertion. Dans ce cadre, le 3FPT a annoncé la prochaine remise d’attestations à 800 femmes formées à Gossas. De l’information à l’insertion Aux côtés du 3FPT, la Direction de l’Emploi participe à cette mobilisation qui se poursuit jusqu’au 21 septembre. Les deux structures partagent une même démarche : rapprocher les services publics des populations et faciliter l’accès à l’information, à la formation et aux dispositifs d’insertion. La rencontre s’est tenue en présence du Directeur général de l’Emploi, de l’Inspecteur de la Jeunesse, des responsables et représentants de l’ODCAV, de la Zone 1 et des ASC de Gossas, ainsi que des représentantes des GIE de femmes de Diandéré. À travers ces 72 Heures, Gossas devient ainsi un espace d’échanges entre les populations et les acteurs de la formation et de l’emploi. Une démarche de proximité qui vise à transformer l’information en opportunités concrètes pour les jeunes et les femmes. Papa Abdoulaye Sy

items.title: Dangote Refinery IPO: Investors to reap bountiful returns, says Devakumar
items.description: By Udeme Akpan The Vice President, Oil and Gas, Dangote Industries Limited, Mr. Edwin Devakumar, has assured prospective investors that the ongoing Initial Public Offering (IPO) of the Dangote Petroleum Refinery presents an opportunity to participate in one of Africa’s most strategic industrial enterprises, saying investors stand to enjoy significant value appreciation and attractive returns over the long term. Mr. Devakumar said the refinery’s strong operational performance, growing market share, robust demand outlook and strategic position within Africa’s energy value chain make it an attractive investment proposition for institutional and retail investors. According to him, the refinery has started making profits and was established to reduce Nigeria’s dependence on imported refined petroleum products, strengthen national energy security, conserve foreign exchange, create employment opportunities and position the country as a major exporter of petroleum products to regional and global markets. “The Dangote Refinery is one of the most significant industrial investments ever undertaken on the African continent. It addresses a critical gap in the energy sector while creating substantial economic value. Those investing in the refinery’s ongoing IPO are investing in a business with strong fundamentals, enormous growth potential and a proven capacity to generate sustainable returns,” Mr. Devakumar said. According to him, “The objective is not merely to raise capital. It is to democratise ownership of a strategic national asset and allow millions of Nigerians and global investors to participate in the value being created by the refinery. We believe this is an opportunity for investors to become partners in Africa’s industrial transformation story.” Mr. Devakumar said funds realised from the offering would support the company’s long-term growth initiatives, operational optimisation, expansion projects, working capital requirements and strategic investments across the petroleum value chain. He emphasised that the refinery’s integrated business model, advanced technologies, large-scale production capacity, deep-water port infrastructure and extensive logistics network provide competitive advantages that are difficult to replicate elsewhere in Africa. “The refinery is strategically positioned to serve domestic, regional and international markets. Demand for refined petroleum products across Africa continues to grow, and our scale, efficiency and location provide a unique advantage in capturing these opportunities. This translates directly into long-term value creation for shareholders,” he stated. Mr. Devakumar explained that the refinery’s ability to process a wide range of crude oil grades, coupled with its production of petrol, diesel, aviation fuel, liquefied petroleum gas and petrochemical feedstocks, has created multiple revenue streams that, he said, strengthen the company’s earnings potential. He further stated that the company remains committed to high standards of corporate governance, transparency, financial discipline, environmental stewardship and operational excellence, which he described as critical to sustaining investor confidence and shareholder value. Once the IPO is concluded and the shares listed, he said the company’s commitment to accountability and transparency would become even stronger. “Investors will benefit from regular financial disclosures, strict governance standards and a management team focused on driving sustainable growth and profitability,” he said. Mr. Devakumar expressed confidence that the refinery’s future earnings potential, expanding export footprint and strategic role in Africa’s energy security would continue to attract investor interest. “This IPO represents more than an investment opportunity; it is an invitation to participate in a historic enterprise that is redefining the African energy landscape. We are confident that investors who subscribe to the offer will be well-positioned to reap bountiful returns as the refinery continues its growth journey and delivers value to shareholders,” he concluded. items.title: 2027: Sowunmi mobilises grassroots for Tinubu’s re-election
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Convener of The Alternative Movement and chieftain of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Otunba Segun Sowunmi, at the weekend commenced grassroots mobilisation in Ogun State in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s re-election bid in the 2027 presidential election. Sowunmi, who spoke during a grassroots mobilisation programme in the Itoko area of Abeokuta South local government area of the State capital, said he was backing President Bola Tinubu because he believed the administration’s economic direction and policy choices were moving the country towards greater fiscal capacity. According to him, Nigeria needs continuity in governance and sufficient time for governments to implement long-term policies, rather than changing direction every four years. “We are here because I have chosen this day, in my capacity as a very strong grassroots leader here in Ogun State, especially as the promoter and convener of the Alternative Movement,” he said. Sowunmi said he had consistently defended the economic policies of the Tinubu administration over the past years, arguing that a government needed adequate resources to execute its programmes. “I have been screaming and shouting that the economic direction, the policy ideas, and the things that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is doing are in the right direction for the country,” he said. “You cannot run a nation on an agenda that says the country will not have money. Because if you don’t have money, what will you even be able to do?” He claimed that increased revenues had created more resources at the federal, state and local government levels, and argued that the development process required policy stability. Sowunmi said Nigeria should embrace what he described as the “principle of the pendulum”, under which political power alternates between the northern and southern parts of the country. “I believe that, for us to be able to make this country a great nation and to hold it together, we must respect the principle of the pendulum,” he said. “If it is the time of the Northern Protectorate, they should bring us a candidate we’ll take. If it is the time of the Southern Protectorate, they should give us a candidate we’ll take.” He argued that democratic governance and policy implementation required continuity, citing countries such as Singapore and Malaysia as examples of nations that, in his view, achieved development through consensus and sustained policy direction. “We cannot be changing leadership every four years. Democracy is very difficult, and the ability to implement policy requires a bit of time,” he said. Sowunmi said the mobilisation would begin at the polling-unit level, with further engagements planned across the State. He added that he planned to proceed with local government-level mobilisation before taking the campaign to the six local government areas in Ogun Central Senatorial District. Sowunmi also said he would mobilise his political structure in Ijebu and other parts of the state in support of Tinubu. “I will go and raise that structure and tell them that it has to be Bola Tinubu and nothing else,” he said. ‘Tinubu has an advantage in Southwest’ Sowunmi argued that political actors seeking the presidency outside what he considers the current political cycle should not underestimate Tinubu’s position. “There is something called the principle of the planets. You will never see the moon and the stars come out when the sun is out,” he said. “Anybody, especially from the Yoruba nation, who is calling himself anything when the sun is out is wasting his time.” He further urged Yoruba voters to support Tinubu, arguing that the region should not be outperformed by other parts of the country in the number of votes cast for the President. “I have come home to beg my people, Yoruba people, that you will not be ashamed,” he said. “Because when the election is over and the people of the North-East, the North-West, and the North-Central produce more votes than you, then where will you put your face?” Sowunmi also compared the 1999 and 2003 presidential elections, arguing that political fortunes could change significantly between election cycles. “We are back to 2003. You did not give Obasanjo a significant number of votes in 1999, but by 2003, everything belonged to him,” he said. Sowunmi said his support for Tinubu was also connected to his belief that Nigeria should avoid what he described as unnecessary political disruption. “I am one of the people who worked very hard to ensure that we can have an arrangement of the pendulum. But right now, we can’t take unnecessary risks,” he said. He also defended the principle of political rotation, recalling that former President Muhammadu Buhari, from the North, served two terms before Tinubu emerged as president in 2023. “If power is in the North, Buhari did eight years. We did not disturb him,” he said. “Now our son is there, breaking his back, breaking his head, working so hard, readjusting the country, doing all the things that need to be done.” Sowunmi also criticised proposals that he believes would amount to a return to policies of the past, particularly regarding fuel subsidy. “We have tried subsidy in this country. We started studying it from 1973, and between 1973 and date, we have seen the result. If it had worked, wouldn’t we have seen it?” He also cited the rehabilitation of Nigeria’s refineries and the emergence of private-sector refining as part of his argument for continuing with the current direction of economic reforms. “We have seen that nothing has worked,” he said. “They couldn’t even repair the refinery for so many years, and one private-sector person has run a refinery.” Sowunmi urged Nigerians to look forward rather than return to policies he considers unsuccessful. “No! We have left Egypt. Forward ever, backward never,” he said. The post 2027: Sowunmi mobilises grassroots for Tinubu’s re-election appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: T-bills auction: Government fails to achieve target; yield on 91-day-bill remains unchanged
items.description: For the first time in over two months, the government failed to achieve its treasury bills target. According to auction results by the Bank of Ghana, the government’s target was marginally undersubscribed. The government received GH¢3.9 billion from the investors, but accepted about GH¢1.8 billion of the bids tendered. The target for the auction was estimated at GH¢4.1 billion. The 91-day bill was the most subscribed, as GH¢2.28 billion of the bids were tendered, representing 57.8% of the total bids. However, the bids accepted were GH¢1.8 billion. The 364-day bill saw bids of about GH¢1.2 billion tendered. The uptake was GH¢110.52 million. For the 182-day bill, GH¢452.79 million of the bids were tendered. The bids accepted were estimated to the tune of GH¢110.52 billion. Meanwhile, interest rates went down across the 182-day and 364-day bills. For the 182-day bill, it declined by 3.0 basis points to 6.48%, whilst it decreased to 9.98% from 10.10% the previous week. However, the yield on the 91-day bill remained unchanged at 4.69%.
